guided.title: Stack two tables
guided.prompt: Stack `a` and `b` into one table with a fresh index 0 to 3 and print it with `print(both.to_string())`.
guided.starter:
import pandas as pd
a = pd.DataFrame({"id": [1, 2], "v": [5, 6]})
b = pd.DataFrame({"id": [3, 4], "v": [7, 8]})
print(a.to_string())
guided.solution:
import pandas as pd
a = pd.DataFrame({"id": [1, 2], "v": [5, 6]})
b = pd.DataFrame({"id": [3, 4], "v": [7, 8]})
both = pd.concat([a, b], ignore_index=True)
print(both.to_string())
hints: Without extra options the row labels repeat; one option renumbers them.

guided.title: Sum pivot
guided.prompt: Build a pivot table of the total `amount` with `region` as rows and `product` as columns, empty cells as 0. Print it with `print(grid.to_string())`.
guided.starter:
import pandas as pd
s = pd.DataFrame({"region": ["N", "S", "N", "S"], "product": ["pen", "pen", "ink", "pen"], "amount": [1, 2, 3, 4]})
print(s.to_string())
guided.solution:
import pandas as pd
s = pd.DataFrame({"region": ["N", "S", "N", "S"], "product": ["pen", "pen", "ink", "pen"], "amount": [1, 2, 3, 4]})
grid = s.pivot_table(index="region", columns="product", values="amount", aggfunc="sum", fill_value=0)
print(grid.to_string())
hints: The default aggregation is the mean, so name the one you want.
guided.expected:
product  ink  pen
region           
N          3    1
S          0    6

guided.title: Shares with crosstab
guided.prompt: Print a crosstab of `plan` (rows) against `churned` (columns) where each row holds shares that add up to 1, rounded to 2 places, with `print(ct.to_string())`.
guided.starter:
import pandas as pd
c = pd.DataFrame({"plan": ["free", "free", "free", "pro", "pro"], "churned": ["yes", "yes", "no", "no", "no"]})
print(pd.crosstab(c["plan"], c["churned"]).to_string())
guided.solution:
import pandas as pd
c = pd.DataFrame({"plan": ["free", "free", "free", "pro", "pro"], "churned": ["yes", "yes", "no", "no", "no"]})
ct = pd.crosstab(c["plan"], c["churned"], normalize="index").round(2)
print(ct.to_string())
hints: `normalize` turns counts into proportions; one value makes each row sum to 1.
guided.expected:
churned    no   yes
plan               
free     0.33  0.67
pro      1.00  0.00

guided.title: Melt months
guided.prompt: Melt `wide` into a long table with columns `store`, `month` and `sales`. Print `print(long.to_string(index=False))`.
guided.starter:
import pandas as pd
wide = pd.DataFrame({"store": ["A", "B"], "jan": [5, 7], "feb": [6, 8]})
print(wide.to_string(index=False))
guided.solution:
import pandas as pd
wide = pd.DataFrame({"store": ["A", "B"], "jan": [5, 7], "feb": [6, 8]})
long = pd.melt(wide, id_vars="store", var_name="month", value_name="sales")
print(long.to_string(index=False))
hints: `id_vars` names the columns that stay as they are.
`var_name` and `value_name` name the two new columns.
guided.expected:
store month  sales
    A   jan      5
    B   jan      7
    A   feb      6
    B   feb      8

independent.title: Combine files and total by region
independent.prompt: Three regional tables `n`, `s`, `w` each have `product` and `amount`. Stack them with a `region` column that records the source (add the column yourself with `assign` before stacking). Print the pivot table of total amount with `product` as rows and `region` as columns (0 for missing), then the number of rows of the stacked table on the last line.
independent.starter:
import pandas as pd
n = pd.DataFrame({"product": ["pen", "ink"], "amount": [10, 20]})
s = pd.DataFrame({"product": ["pen"], "amount": [5]})
w = pd.DataFrame({"product": ["ink", "pad"], "amount": [7, 9]})
print(len(n))
independent.solution:
import pandas as pd
n = pd.DataFrame({"product": ["pen", "ink"], "amount": [10, 20]})
s = pd.DataFrame({"product": ["pen"], "amount": [5]})
w = pd.DataFrame({"product": ["ink", "pad"], "amount": [7, 9]})
all_ = pd.concat([n.assign(region="N"), s.assign(region="S"), w.assign(region="W")], ignore_index=True)
print(all_.pivot_table(index="product", columns="region", values="amount", aggfunc="sum", fill_value=0).to_string())
print(len(all_))
independent.expected:
region    N  S  W
product          
ink      20  0  7
pad       0  0  9
pen      10  5  0
5

independent.title: Wide to long and back
independent.prompt: Melt `wide` (columns `item`, `q1`, `q2`, `q3`) into `item`, `quarter`, `units`. Print the quarter with the highest total units and its total as `q2 66` style (quarter name, space, total). Then pivot the long table back with `pivot_table` (sum) and print `grid.loc["pen", "q3"]`.
independent.starter:
import pandas as pd
wide = pd.DataFrame({"item": ["pen", "ink", "pad"], "q1": [10, 20, 5], "q2": [30, 25, 11], "q3": [12, 22, 9]})
print(wide.shape)
independent.solution:
import pandas as pd
wide = pd.DataFrame({"item": ["pen", "ink", "pad"], "q1": [10, 20, 5], "q2": [30, 25, 11], "q3": [12, 22, 9]})
long = pd.melt(wide, id_vars="item", var_name="quarter", value_name="units")
totals = long.groupby("quarter")["units"].sum()
print(totals.idxmax(), totals.max())
grid = long.pivot_table(index="item", columns="quarter", values="units", aggfunc="sum")
print(grid.loc["pen", "q3"])

independent.title: Stretch: row shares and a check
independent.prompt: From `o` (columns `country`, `status`), print a crosstab of counts with an `All` margin row and column (`margins=True`), then print for each country the share of orders with status `returned`, rounded to 2 places, as `country share` lines in alphabetical order of country.
independent.starter:
import pandas as pd
o = pd.DataFrame({"country": ["UK", "UK", "UK", "US", "US", "DE"], "status": ["shipped", "returned", "shipped", "returned", "returned", "shipped"]})
print(len(o))
independent.solution:
import pandas as pd
o = pd.DataFrame({"country": ["UK", "UK", "UK", "US", "US", "DE"], "status": ["shipped", "returned", "shipped", "returned", "returned", "shipped"]})
print(pd.crosstab(o["country"], o["status"], margins=True).to_string())
share = pd.crosstab(o["country"], o["status"], normalize="index")["returned"].round(2)
for country, v in share.items():
    print(country, v)
independent.expected:
status   returned  shipped  All
country                        
DE              0        1    1
UK              1        2    3
US              2        0    2
All             3        3    6
DE 0.0
UK 0.33
US 1.0

checks.question: `jan` and `feb` each have 2 rows with labels 0 and 1. What are the labels of `pd.concat([jan, feb])`?
checks.explanation: Without `ignore_index=True` each table keeps its own labels, so they repeat: 0, 1, 0, 1. Renumbering to 0 to 3 needs `ignore_index=True`.

checks.question: A pivot table of amounts shows values that look too small. No `aggfunc` was given. What is the likely cause?
options: The default aggregation is the mean, not the sum
checks.explanation: The default `aggfunc` is `mean`, so each cell is an average of the rows for that pair. Pass `aggfunc="sum"` for totals. The other options do not change how cells are computed.

checks.question: `wide` has 4 products and 3 month columns. How many rows does `pd.melt(wide, id_vars='product')` have?
checks.explanation: Each product is repeated once for every melted column: 4 times 3 gives 12 rows. Four would be the row count of the wide table, and 7 adds instead of multiplies.

checks.question: What does `pd.crosstab(a, b, normalize='index')` return in each row?
checks.explanation: `normalize="index"` divides each cell by its row total, so each row sums to 1. Dividing by the grand total is `normalize="all"`.

checks.question: You stack the same monthly file twice with `concat`. What happens to duplicates?
checks.explanation: `concat` never removes duplicates; it only stacks. Use `duplicated` or `drop_duplicates` (Day 75) to detect and remove them.
